about: Headless bot playtests of Lure v6 (camera-centred flight, death wave, death walls, flying asteroids), 20 runs per cell on the final tuning. Bots are skill proxies, not taste proxies. 'random' = no-skill floor; 'evader' = crude competent player: flees and swirls toward the lane middle, dodges telegraphs, keeps off rocks/walls, pushes right (harder when the wave is close). arena = mean sector reached (of 6). Course = 6 x 3600px.
tuning_history: Pursuers at their arena speed (168 px/s, vs your 270) could never catch you in a forward flight: the evader won 20/20 in ~58s by holding right. Flight chasers now fly at 300 (configurable per stage): you can't outrun them, only shed them, as in reference moment 2.
Field ~2x denser and sectors 2400 -> 3600px so the flight takes minutes (P9), not a 60s sprint.
Apparent 'death wall' deaths turned out to be a bot artifact (its swirl always turned the same way, steering into the bottom wall). Fixed in the bot; wall deaths dropped to ~1 in 30.

A/B difficulty: at equal density, drifting (A) reached sector 3.4 vs tumbling (B) 5.6. A thinner A field made A *worse* (2.65): rocks are lure tools, and fast streams sweep pursuers away. A got a 1.5x denser field instead. Remaining gap 3.6 vs 5.0; B is still somewhat easier for the bot.
notes: A full flight takes the bot ~100-125s; Mikael will likely weave more and take longer (his v5 run reached sector 4 in 144s).
Mikael has out-performed the evader in every version. Treat these numbers as a floor for him.
Death causes for the bot are now mostly rocks and chasers (the core loop), with few walls or wave deaths. The wave is pressure, not the usual killer.
